Differentiate between User Requirements and System Requirements. Explain the IEEE 830 standard structure and qualities of a well-written Software Requirements Specification (SRS) document.
questions.solutionOutline: User requirements written in natural language for non-technical stakeholders; system requirements provide detailed functional specifications for developers. IEEE 830 specifies Introduction, Overall Description, Specific Requirements. Qualities: correct, unambiguous, complete, consistent, verifiable, modifiable, traceable.

questions.text: Draw Level-0 (Context Diagram) and Level-1 Data Flow Diagrams (DFD) for an Online Shopping or Food Delivery System. Clearly identify data stores, external entities, data flows, and transformation processes.
questions.solutionOutline: Level-0 shows external entities (Customer, Vendor, Payment Gateway, Admin) interacting with the central system process. Level-1 explodes into sub-processes: Authentication, Browse Menu/Products, Cart Management, Order Placement, Payment Processing, and Inventory Update with respective data stores.

questions.text: What is Software Inspection? Explain the formal software inspection process (Planning, Overview, Preparation, Inspection Meeting, Rework, Follow-up) and the types of faults uncovered during inspection.
questions.solutionOutline: Formal peer review of software artifacts (code, design, requirements) without executing code. Steps: Planning, Overview meeting, Individual preparation, Inspection meeting with Reader and Scribe, Rework by author, Follow-up verification by Moderator. Detects data faults, control faults, computation faults, and standard violations.

questions.text: Explain Component-Based Software Engineering (CBSE). Differentiate between "CBSE with reuse" and "CBSE for reuse" with neat block diagrams. What is Commercial-Off-The-Shelf (COTS) product integration?
questions.solutionOutline: CBSE focuses on assembling existing software components rather than building from scratch. CBSE for reuse develops generic, reusable software components. CBSE with reuse integrates reusable components into a target system. COTS involves integrating packaged commercial software into custom business systems.

questions.text: Define Version, Variant, and Release with respect to Software Configuration Management (SCM). Explain version numbering schemes and workspace baseline control.
questions.solutionOutline: Version is an instance of a configuration item that differs from other instances. Variant represents alternative versions coexisting simultaneously for different operating systems or hardware. Release is a version distributed to external customers. SCM tracks baselines and branching.

questions.text: Compare the Waterfall Model, Incremental Model, and Spiral Model of software development. Under what project characteristics, team sizes, and risk profiles is each model most suitable?
questions.solutionOutline: Waterfall: linear sequential, well-defined unchanging requirements, low risk. Incremental: delivers operational chunks iteratively, accommodating early user feedback. Spiral: risk-driven iterative model with four quadrants (objectives, risk analysis, engineering, review) suited for large, complex, mission-critical systems.

questions.text: What is System Architecture? Explain the Call-and-Return architecture and Pipe-and-Filter architectural patterns with suitable block diagrams, use cases, and trade-offs.
questions.solutionOutline: System architecture defines high-level structure, components, relationships, and principles of design. Call-and-Return uses main program and subroutines or RPCs for structured control. Pipe-and-Filter streams data through independent processing filters connected by pipes, ideal for Unix pipelines and data transformations.

questions.text: Define Periodic and Aperiodic stimuli in real-time embedded systems. What are the key architectural components and timing constraints in a real-time data acquisition system?
questions.solutionOutline: Periodic stimuli occur at predictable, regular time intervals (e.g., sensor sampling at 100 Hz). Aperiodic stimuli occur unpredictably in response to external events (e.g., emergency alarm interrupts). Real-time data acquisition collects analog inputs via ADC, buffers, processes, and drives actuators within deterministic deadline limits.

questions.text: What is Software Quality Assurance (SQA)? Differentiate between SEI Capability Maturity Model (CMM/CMMI) and ISO 9001 software quality frameworks.
questions.solutionOutline: SQA comprises planned and systematic pattern of actions to ensure high quality in software processes and products. CMMI is domain-specific to software engineering with 5 progressive maturity levels. ISO 9001 is a generic quality management standard certifying that documented processes are consistently followed.

questions.text: Explain Integration Testing and compare Top-down, Bottom-up, Big-Bang, and Sandwich (Hybrid) integration testing strategies with suitable diagrams, stubs, and test drivers.
questions.solutionOutline: Integration testing verifies interfaces between interacting software modules. Big-bang tests all combined modules at once (high isolation difficulty). Top-down starts at main control module using stubs for subordinates. Bottom-up tests atomic modules first using driver harnesses. Sandwich combines top-down and bottom-up.

questions.text: What is Feasibility Study in Requirements Engineering? Explain Technical, Operational, Economic, and Legal feasibility analysis in detail.
questions.solutionOutline: Feasibility study evaluates whether the proposed software project is practical and viable before committing substantial financial resources. Evaluates: Technical (availability of technology/skills), Operational (organizational fit and user acceptance), Economic (cost-benefit ROI analysis), and Legal/Contractual compliance.

questions.text: Explain Function Point (FP) analysis as a software size and cost estimation metric. How are Unadjusted Function Points (UFP) and Value Adjustment Factor (VAF) calculated from 14 General System Characteristics (GSC)?
questions.solutionOutline: FP measures functional size independent of programming language. Identifies 5 functional components: External Inputs (EI), External Outputs (EO), External Inquiries (EQ), Internal Logical Files (ILF), and External Interface Files (EIF). FP = UFP * (0.65 + 0.01 * sum(Fi)), where Fi are 14 GSC ratings from 0 to 5.

questions.text: What is Software Maintenance? Distinguish between Corrective, Adaptive, Perfective, and Preventive maintenance with examples. Why does maintenance consume over 60% of total lifecycle cost?
questions.solutionOutline: Modification of software product after delivery to fix bugs, improve performance, or adapt to a changed environment. Corrective (bug fixing), Adaptive (OS/hardware porting), Perfective (feature enhancement requested by users), Preventive (refactoring for maintainability). High cost due to architectural decay, lack of documentation, and regression side effects.

questions.text: What is Agile Software Development? Explain the core principles of Agile Manifesto and describe the Scrum framework including Product Backlog, Sprint, Daily Scrum, Sprint Review, and Retrospective.
questions.solutionOutline: Iterative, incremental, human-centric development philosophy emphasizing rapid working software delivery, customer collaboration, and adapting to change. Scrum roles: Product Owner, Scrum Master, Developers. Artifacts: Product Backlog, Sprint Backlog, Increment. Ceremonies: Sprint Planning, Daily Stand-up, Sprint Review, Retrospective.
